title: Quality Ops Lighthouse — Weekly Onboarding Regression Synthesis (2026-05-20)
body:
TL;DR:
This weekly synthesis collects onboarding evaluation signals, a compact hotlist of failing promptsets, and agreed immediate action items for the next 7 days. The goal: keep model rollouts (hosted + dedicated) from regressing user-facing metrics while we expand promptset coverage for new verticals.

Summary of trends (May 13–May 20):
- Aggregate quality score (opinionated composite) slipped 3.4 points week-over-week. Primary driver: a rise in hallucination_rate for 2LLM-v2 on long-form instructions.
- Latency and cost stable; no infra regressions detected.
- Coverage gap identified: 8 promptsets from enterprise-search vertical show brittle grounding behavior under retrieval-augmented prompts.

Important context and signal sources:
- Data: onboarding eval batches (EVAL-233) + production shadow traces for newly onboarded customers.
- Metrics used: semantic-fidelity (clf-based), hallucination_rate (manual + classifier), instruction-follow-rate, BLEU/ROUGE for structured tasks, latency p95.
- Canary: traffic shadowing to 2LLM-v2 on dedicated pools (canary id: APLML-987).

Top failure modes this week (short descriptions + triage owner):
1) Hallucination on multi-step instructions (owner: Marcus Nguyen)
   - Symptoms: model invents entities when user supplies partial facts; rate jumped from 1.8% -> 6.6% for >3-step tasks.
   - Representative prompt (enterprise-search): \"Given doc snippets, synthesize a single-line taxonomy mapping\" -> model fabricates categories not present.
   - Proposed immediate mitigation: enable prefix-KV caching + retrieval-scope guard; temp rollback to 2LLM-v1 for high-risk routes.

2) Numeric misformatting in tabular summarization (owner: Claire O'Connell)
   - Symptoms: currency rounding errors and misplaced delimiters for locale-sensitive tests.
   - Example promptset: invoices-coverage-22; fail mode classified as formatting drift.
   - Mitigation: augment promptset with explicit \"format as CSV with two decimals\" and add deterministic post-format validator.

3) Retrieval mismatch (owner: Diego Ramirez)
   - Symptoms: RAG pipeline returns stale passages; model prefers newer docs leading to conflicting answers.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: retrieval index refresh latency + scorer weight change in infra release INFRA-412.
   - Action: roll back scorer change in infra canary and re-run retrieval-heavy promptsets.

Promptset hotlist (priority order):
- P0: enterprise-search/multi-step-taxonomy (covering hallucination spikes) — blocked tests: 48/200 failing.
- P0: invoices-coverage-22 (numeric formatting) — failing: 13/50 examples flagged by validator.
- P1: rAG-freshness-batch (staleness) — intermittent fails across regions.
- P2: dialog-persona-stability (persona drift under long context) — exploratory triage scheduled.

Action items (owner, due):
- Marcus: Run augmented hallucination classifier sweep across last 14 days of prod shadow traces; produce a signal heatmap by promptset. Due: 2026-05-24. Linked: APLML-1012.
- Claire: Patch formatting validator and push PR with updated prompt recipes for invoices-coverage-22. Due: 2026-05-22. GitHub: PR #329.
- Diego + infra: Revert scorer change in canary region eu-west-1; reindex retrieval corpus for impacted customers. Due: 2026-05-21. Jira: INFRA-412 rollback.
- Ops: Temporarily pin hosted-api route /v1/chat for impacted customers to 2LLM-v1 until signal passes (canary gating). Due: 2026-05-21.

Short-term rollout plan (7 days):
1) Hold broad rollout of 2LLM-v2 for routes with P0 promptsets.
2) Deploy fixes for formatting validator and re-run local promptset suite (Claire).
3) If hallucination classifier's FDR < 5% after mitigations, re-enable canary traffic at 25% for 3 days and monitor.

Evaluation and monitoring checklist to attach to rollouts:
- Pre-rollout: baseline metric snapshot (semantic-fidelity, hallucination_rate, p95 latency).
- Daily: automated promptset runner results, top-10 failing examples exported to shared S3.
- Post-rollout: 72h signal review; if any P0 metric regresses by >2 points, rollback.

Open questions (for weekly sync):
- Do we need a stricter gating rule for retrieval-influenced promptsets? Current gating is signal-level, not promptset-level.
- Should we expand the hallucination classifier training set with adversarial negative examples from enterprise-search?

Meeting agenda (weekly triage — Thu 10:30am PT):
- Quick status: P0 hotlist (5m)
- Owners give updates on action items (15m)
- Infrastructure notes: retrieval/scoring rollout plan (10m)
- Risk decisions: pin/rollback/continue (10m)
- AOB + blockers (10m)

Appendix (notes-to-self style):
- Quick list of tickets to check: EVAL-233 (onboarding batch run), APLML-987 (canary config), INFRA-412 (retrieval scorer), APLML-1012 (hallucination sweep).
- Quick commands: \"eval-run --promptset enterprise-search/multi-step-taxonomy --limit 200 --output s3://redwood-eval/onboard-2026-05-20\"
- Slack threads: #onboard-regression (pin: summary, artifacts), #infra-rollouts (pin: INFRA-412 discussion).

Notes on style and next draft: keep this doc lean and actionable. In the next edition we'll add a compact visual (heatmap) and link to the failing-example bundle. If anything changes before Thu sync, update the action rows and bump last_modified.

End of synthesis.
